stem: A CPU-bound Lambda function runs slowly at its current 512 MB memory setting, and the team wants to shorten its execution duration without changing any code.

choices.text: Set reserved concurrency for the function
Increase the function's memory setting toward 1,769 MB or higher

rationale: Lambda allocates CPU power linearly with the configured memory, reaching the equivalent of one full vCPU at 1,769 MB, so raising memory toward or beyond that point gives a CPU-bound function more compute and can shorten its execution duration with no code change. Provisioned concurrency pre-initializes execution environments to remove cold-start latency; it does not change the CPU available to an already-running invocation. Lambda SnapStart resumes new environments from a cached, already-initialized snapshot to cut cold starts; it does not add CPU power to a running function either. Reserved concurrency sets a floor and ceiling on how many invocations can run at once; it has no effect on how fast any single invocation executes.
